title: OurLegacy - Turn your family story into a keepsake book
page_key: ourlegacy.family/ | Your story becomes a book starring your family.

output.observation: The OurLegacy home page explains that users can write a family story, upload photos, and turn it into a premium hardcover keepsake book. It prominently offers free starter credits, lists a $59 Family Storybook, and includes links for pricing, questions, safety, signing in, and creating a storybook.
output.think_aloud: This is a very clear introduction, and the photograph is warm and inviting. I can see that I should not need to put in card details to start, but I want to understand the $5 free credits and the difference between creating a story and ordering a physical book before I commit. The words “premium hardcover” and the $59 price are prominent, which is helpful, although I would still like to read the smaller details carefully.

site_model.what_it_is: A website for turning a family memory into an illustrated storybook and, if wanted, a printed keepsake book.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Parents and relatives who want to create a personalised story featuring their family for a child.
site_model.value_proposition: It turns a real family story and photos into a personal storybook starring the family, with a downloadable PDF and private sharing option, and can be printed as a premium hardcover.
main_tasks: Write or describe a family memory
Upload photos to personalise the characters
Choose the reading age and story details
Download the digital version or order a printed keepsake
site_model.pricing_model: The page says there is $5 in free credits, with no card needed, and that generating new story drafts costs $1 in credits. A Family Storybook hardcover is listed at $59, with extra books costing $35 each. The Family Tribute Book and Film is marked coming soon and listed at $149.
trust_signals: The site says photos are used only to make characters, never sold, and never used to train public models.
It says photos can be deleted at any time.
It says stories are reviewed against child-safety guidelines.
It clearly states that users set the reading age.
It says the company is new and does not pretend to have reviews it does not have.
It states that no card is needed to use the free credits
site_model.fit_for_me: This is relevant to me because I want to pass on the story of the blue kite made from an old shirt to Oliver. The idea of a short, age-appropriate illustrated book with our family as the characters sounds lovely, but I will need to check how personal the illustrations will be and what happens to the photos.

page_review.purpose: To introduce the family storybook service, explain its main benefits and pricing, and direct visitors to begin creating a storybook.
page_review.what_is_happening: The home page is fully visible at the top and includes a large introductory message, a button to create a storybook, a warm illustrative image, a short trust and price summary, and links to further information. The announcement bar advertises a free Founding Families Program.
page_review.first_impression: I find the page attractive, calm, and easy to understand at a glance. The large button and the phrase “$5 free to start” make the first step obvious. I am encouraged by the statement that no card is needed.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try creating a storybook because the service seems designed for the family memory I want to share.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the prominent “Create Your Storybook” button and the repeated “Write Your Story” button are very noticeable.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Create Your Storybook” describes what I want to do, although I would still like the following screens to explain the process before asking for information.

issues.title: The free-credit wording may not explain the total cost clearly enough
issues.evidence: The page alternates between “$5 free to start,” “Generate Storybook - $1.00,” and “Family Storybook $59,” while also saying “pay only for the keepsakes you love.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I want to know exactly what I can create and preview with the free credits and what I would have to pay later. The difference between a digital creation and a printed keepsake could otherwise be confusing.
issues.fix: Add one plain sentence or small summary table stating: free credit amount, exact cost per story draft, what remains free, the cost of the PDF, and the separate cost of a printed hardcover.

issues.title: The announcement bar promotes a special programme without explaining its conditions
issues.evidence: “The Founding Families Program — 20 families, free to join, your story first →”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am wary of offers that sound special but do not immediately say what is included, whether I need to qualify, or what happens after the programme.
issues.fix: Explain the programme terms in the announcement itself or link directly to a short, readable explanation of the offer and its limits.

issues.title: Some explanatory text is visually small
issues.evidence: The pricing and trust explanations are presented in smaller grey text beneath the large headings and controls.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I have mild difficulty reading small, low-contrast text, and this is exactly the information I need to read carefully before deciding.
issues.fix: Use at least 16px text, stronger contrast, and avoid making important pricing, privacy, and safety explanations smaller than secondary navigation.

positives: The main call to action is prominent and repeated.
The home page clearly says that no card is needed to start.
The visible price of $59 is not hidden.
The site directly addresses privacy, child safety, and reading age.
The honest note that the company is new and has few reviews is reassuring.
The wording “No fake sales, no countdown timers” avoids some of the pressure I dislike on shopping websites.

output.memory_note: Remember: $5 in free credits, no card needed; generating a new story draft costs $1 in credits; Family Storybook hardcover is listed at $59.
output.plan: I will click “Create Your Storybook” to begin. I will then read the sign-up and story process carefully, use my e-mail address, and stop before entering any payment details or paying real money.
